Om universitetet.md:
Universiteti Europian i Tiranës (European University of Tirana) is a small, private higher education institution located in the urban setting of the medium-sized city of Tirana with a student population of approximately 3000 students.

EUT engages in high quality teaching and research in the following major disciplines: Social Sciences, Journalism and Information, Business and Administration, Law, Information and Communication Technologies. EUT aspires to be a leading university in the development of knowledge in the Albanian society; a centre of excellence in the academic formation of students; a centre of expertise in the social, political, legal, economic and information technology studies in the country with a wider impact in the region and beyond; as well as a centre of excellence in scientific research in EUT´s areas of expertise.

Boende.md:
Most of the international students in Tirana choose to live in private forms of accommodation. Living in a  
private apartment means a greater privacy and less rules and procedures, unfortunately a lower level of  
socialization.

To find a place, you can require support on your hunt from the International Officer or  
Erasmus Buddy in your host institution. A different way is posting your ad for requiring an apartment in  
different portals and in social media groups of the city where you study at – especially Facebook. It is  
advised to use join the Erasmus Student Network group in Facebook, and distribute your posting there,  
while personalizing it for the city you are studying at - Tirana.

Shared apartments and Airbnb: For those who are arriving to Tirana alone, shared apartments with other  
international students of UET are often a good option, as you can live cheaply and meet new people. Living  
in a shared apartment means sharing a kitchen and a bathroom. Please get in touch with other  
international students and stay connected to the international community at UET. Airbnb option tends  
to be more costly, however there are plenty of Airbnb-s which are available to international students.

An international student in Tirana, according to the 2020 estimations, will need around 550 EUR/month  
in order to meet the necessary living expenses.  
As the official statistics reveal, international students in Tirana tend to spend about 200-250 € every  
month for their accommodation, apart from the costs of living. If the student decides to share the  
accommodation, that the cost would be lower.  
However, if you prefer to get a fully furnished apartment, you should expect to pay a higher rent. For  
example, in Tirana you can expect to spend around 400 – 500€ for a fully furnished apartment including  
bills.

Om orten.md:
Adelaide is a vibrant city, known for its festivals, cultural diversity and major sporting events. It also has a good mix of shopping, beaches and cafes in all price ranges. The city balances city life with beautiful countryside, and close links to other regions of South Australia. Enjoy Instagram-friendly beaches like Glenelg, a coastline that stretches as far as the eye can see, great wine in the Adelaide Hills, and the beauty of Kangaroo Island – you’ll never run out of things to do or  
places to visit. Ranked the 9th most liveable city globally by The Economist Intelligence Unit, Adelaide stands out with a perfect score of 100 in education—making it an exceptional place to live and learn.

Språkkrav.md:
C in Engelska 6 or Engelska 7 from Upper Secondary School. Must not be older than 5 years.  
Letter from Unit for International Mobility confirming C1 level is accepted.  
[Entry requirements)](https://www.adelaide.edu.au/inbound-study-abroad/steps-to-apply/entry-requirements)

If English is not your first language, you may need a valid Academic IELTS, TOEFL iBT, or other approved test of English. :  
• IELTS - minimum overall score of 6.5, with no individual band less than 6.0,  
• TOEFL iBT - minimum overall score of 79, and sub-scores of 21 for writing, 18 for speaking, 13 for reading, and 12 for listening.  
Note: Some study areas may require a higher English language score

For a comprehensive list of all English language evidence accepted by Adelaide University, please visit the [English language proficiency webpage](https://adelaideuni.edu.au/study/international-students/how-to-apply/entry-requirements/english-language-proficiency/#accordion-66ccd17d09-item-59d8904657).  
We may also accept alternative ways of demonstrating English proficiency for entry into the study abroad and exchange programs.  
Students should remain aware of the [English language visa requirements](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/help-support/meeting-our-requirements/english-language) determined by the Australian Department of Home Affairs and how this may differ from University entry requirements.

Students are covered through the Swedish State's Insurance (Kammarkollegiet) Student UT.

Exceptions from the requirement of OSHC (Overseas Student Health Cover) apply to Swedish students that are covered by Kammarkollegiet, plus Norwegian and Belgian students. Om orten.md:
Nicknamed “the Bush Capital”, Canberra is  
the political and administrative centre of Australia. Unique among  
world capitals, Canberra is a small, vibrant city nestled amongst some  
of the country’s most beautiful natural environments. Explore Canberra for Australian culture and history at superb monuments and galleries in this city surrounded by parklands and native bushland. Visit Parliament House, the Australian War Memorial, National Gallery of Australia and Questacon. Experience the the Balloon Fiesta in autumn, Fireside Festival in winter, and Floriade in spring. Explore the Australian Alps or Tidnbinbilla Nature Reserve and Murrumbidgee River Corridor, just a short drive away.

Språkkrav.md:
VG/MVG in Engelska C is required or a grade of C in Engelska 7 according to the new Upper Secondary grades (GY2011). This must have been completed  
no more than two years prior to the date of application.

If Uppsala University is able to provide a letter to confirm students satisfy a C1 level comprehension in reading, writing, speaking and listening via the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages System (CEFR), students can use this to meet the requirement.

If you have studied a program at UU completely taught in English for at least two years (120 earned UU credits) at the time of the application to ANU, a letter from your program coordinator/department at UU and your transcript may be accepted to fulfill the language requirements.

[English language admission requirements](https://policies.anu.edu.au/ppl/document/ANUP_6546951)

Study abroad or exchange applicants to the ANU College of Law must have an overall score of C2 with no less than C2 in each of reading and writing and no less than C1 in speaking and listening according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages System.

Students should remain aware of the English language visa requirements determined by the Australian Department of Home Affairs and how this may differ from University entry requirements.

Om universitetet.md:
From a single campus in Melbourne with just 400 students in 1961, Monash has grown into an ecosystem of campuses, education centres and partnerships spanning the globe. With approximately 60,000 students (and 290,000 alumni) from over 170 countries, Monash is now Australia's largest university. A global university with a presence on four continents and ambitious plans for the future.The youngest member of the prestigious Group of Eight, Monash has fostered a strong record of innovation through research collaboration and engagement with industry.

Students and staff are filled with enterprising capabilities, a result of enduring partnerships with government and industry. The focus is always on how to empower people to make a significant impact for the betterment of communities. Things like the bionic eye, the anti-flu drug Relenza and the Inhaled Oxytocin project are changing lives.Learning at Monash is supported by an outward looking curriculum, multifaceted modes of delivery, flexible and purposeful learning spaces, and opportunities to develop a range of practical skills. Students are prepared for the future that awaits, whatever path they choose.

Om orten.md: UQ has campuses in and around Brisbane, the capital city of the state of Queensland. Brisbane is the third largest city in Australia, after Sydney and Melbourne, with a multicultural population of 2.1 million. Built on and around the hills overlooking the Brisbane River, the city is characterised by a subtropical climate, a safe and relaxed outdoor lifestyle, unique “Queenslander” architecture, bustling restaurants and cafés, and thriving arts, sports and entertainment scenes. Brisbane has all the advantages of a large modern city — cafés, restaurants, bars, galleries, museums, sporting events, and shopping districts — yet retains the friendliness and charm of a small regional town. Queensland’s landscape comprises lush northern rainforests, red deserts in the west, and golden surf beaches in the south-east. It is also home to the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef on the planet and one of the seven wonders of the natural world.

Boende.md:
Students have three main accommodation options:
- If you want to arrange your accommodation ahead of time, have your meals catered for you and lots of support and activities at your fingertips, you should consider living in a Residential College. However, spaces at the Colleges are very limited and in high demand. You will need to apply early and are not guaranteed a place.
- If you want to be a little more independent (or are unsuccessful at securing a place in a College) but still want to have your accommodation arranged before you arrive, you should consider living in off-campus student housing. This is self-catered, furnished accommodation designed for students and can be booked online from overseas. Preferred providers are listed on the website.
- The third option is to book temporary accommodation and wait until you arrive in Brisbane to secure permanent accommodation. If you choose this option, you should plan to arrive in Brisbane at least two to three weeks before the start of Orientation as it can take some time to find a suitable place and get settled in. This option offers the widest variety of choices and prices.

For more [information on accommodation](https://study.uq.edu.au/study-options/study-abroad)

Språkkrav.md:
The Swedish Upper Secondary School Leaving Certificate (gymnasiebetyg) must be undertaken no more than ten (10) years prior to the commencement o study at UNSW. VG/MVG in Engelska B or Engelska C is required. Or a grade D in English in the final year (English 6/English Course B) (GY2011).  
(The same exemption applies on Upper Secondary School Leaving Certificates from Denmark, Norway, Germany and Switzerland).

If English  
is not your first language, you will need to provide proof of your English proficiency  
at time of application.  
You can do this  
by providing evidence that you meet on of UNSW’s approved criteria.  
This is currently 6.5 IELTS or 90 TOEFL (iBT) for Exchange students. You are only required to meet the overall  
score for IELTS and TOEFL, you do not need to meet each of the subtests.  
For prior study conditions and other acceptable  
criteria please see [https://www.unsw.edu.au/english-requirements-policy](https://www.unsw.edu.au/english-requirements-policy)

It is important to check you meet our English requirements before being  
nominated by your home university. It is  
too late to sit a test after our application deadline if you don’t meet our entry  
requirements. You should arrange your  
language tests at least 6 months in advance.

Students should remain aware of the [English language visa requirements](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/help-support/meeting-our-requirements/english-language) determined by the Australian Department of Home Affairs and how this may differ from University entry requirements.

Terminsdatum.md:
[Academic Calender](https://www.student.unsw.edu.au/calendar)

It is compulsory to attend the orientation day the week before the semester starts.

The UNSW academic calendar comprises of three terms as well as a Summer Term in January (ST) and Winter (WT) intensive term in August.  
For semester-based programs, you have the choice of 3 courses over a standard Term, or 4 courses over a Double or Tailored Term. For yearlong programs, you can take 8 courses.

Starting in 2028, UNSW will introduce its new flex-semester calendar featuring two semesters. Students applying for a one-year exchange commencing in Tailored Term 3 or Term 3, 2027 (August 2027) will transition from a term-based to a semester-based study structure.

Om universitetet.md:
The University was established in 1850 and the first students were admitted in 1852.

The University of Sydney offers a wide range of academic programs. Students have access to world of possibilities through its international affiliations, industry and alumni mentoring programs and innovative partnerships. The university has a 50,000 member student body including over 10,000 international students representing 145 countries. When it comes to extracurricular activities, students can choose from over 200 clubs and societies, competitive and social sporting teams, two fully equipped fitness centres and a dynamic calendar of on campus events and celebrations.

Students should remain aware of the [English language visa requirements](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/help-support/meeting-our-requirements/english-language) determined by the Australian Department of Home Affairs and how this may differ from University entry requirements.

Språkkrav.md:
1.A minimum grade of VG / C in English from Swedish Upper Secondary School (Gymnasium) is accepted. Currently no limit of how old it can be.

2. University of Western Australia (UWA) can accept a formal letter from the Unit for International Mobility at Uppsala University confirming the medium of instruction (MOI) being English for the applicant’s completed course, if the student:
- Is currently enrolled in a degree fully taught in English
- By the time of their semester/year study commencement at UWA, has completed 2 years of full-time study in English.

If you do not have the required results from Swedish Upper Secondary School or will not have completed 2 years of full-time study in English, a proof of an international language test will be required.

[English language requirements](https://www.uwa.edu.au/study/how-to-apply/english-language-requirements)[Be aware of the](https://www.uow.edu.au/study/study-abroad-exchange/studyabroad/enquire-and-apply/how-to-apply/application-criteria/)[English language visa requirements](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/help-support/meeting-our-requirements/english-language) determined by the Australian Department of Home Affairs and how these may differ from University entry requirements.

Om orten.md: Gent \[ˈgɛnt\]) is a city and a municipality in the Flemish Region of Belgium. It is the capital and largest city of the East Flanders province and after Antwerp the largest municipality of Belgium. Ghent is a 30-minute train ride away from Brussels. Its size (250 000 inhabitants) and position allow the inhabitants to enjoy a city with an interesting crossover between open cosmopolitanism and the quiet atmosphere of a provincial town. Ghent is a city of history as it was one of the richest and most powerful cities in Europe during the Middle Ages and still breathes the atmosphere of a thriving late-medieval city state.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
All subjects at Bachelor's, Master and PhD levels are available, but there are some restrictions.

Most courses in English are on the Master level, so **this is a perfect place to study as a master's student** .

Within the Faculty of Arts, most of the courses in English are at bachelor's level, though.

**At least half of the courses/credits must be from the field of study (subject) of your exchange. The other half can be taken within the same faculty or from another faculty.**  
You need to have completed at least 60 credits at Uppsala University before you start your exchange.

**Please observe that the academic level of courses and the expected input from students is high! Faculty of Law** If you are following a 5-year law program (leading to admission to legal practice) you must be in one of your last two years when coming to the faculty of law.

**Faculty of Economics and Business:** 5 different study fields are offered: Economics, Business Administration, Public Administration and Management, Business Economics and Business Engineering. Courses are instructed at 3rd-year bachelor level and master level. This means that you need to have completed a minimum of 120 ECTS in your home degree by the start of the exchange period, to take bachelor courses and a minimum of 180 ECTS to take part in master courses. You need to be an Economics/Business student at UU so you can fulfil their requirements.

Boende.md:
Exchange students can apply for accommodation in Ghent University’s Halls of Residence. However, the number of rooms is limited, and **accommodation cannot be guaranteed.**

Students are strongly encouraged to apply **as early as possible** after receiving their invitation from Ghent University following their nomination. The first step in the application process is to submit an **Online Learning Agreement.**

Please note that you can only apply for a room in the University Halls of Residence after you have submitted your application as an exchange student to Ghent University.

For information about university accommodation and how to apply, please visit the Ghent University [housing webpage](https://www.ugent.be/en/facilities/housing).

If university accommodation is unavailable, the Ghent University Housing Office can also provide advice and guidance on finding accommodation on the private rental market.

Om orten.md:
The capital of Rio Grande do Sul (RS), Porto Alegre is located in a strategic point for Mercosur. It is situated at equal distance to Buenos Aires and Montevideo, as well as to São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.  
The city has an excellent hotel network, modern shopping malls, theaters, universities and a range of restaurants offering international cuisine.  
The climate in Porto Alegre is considered subtropical, meaning the weather can change quickly and unexpectedly. The city has four well-defined seasons.  
Summers are very hot and winters can get very cold. In the fall, days are shorter and the temperature becomes milder, bringing some days of chilly weather.

Om universitetet.md: The university, founded in 1841, has about 15,000 students and is considered one of the premier research universities in Canada. It is often compared to the character of Yale University in the United States and has very high admission requirements than any other university in Canada. The University takes pride in being a medium-sized university with small classes and a wide range of courses. It is prominent in several fields, including political science, history and art history. Queen's students come from all across Canada and there is a high proportion of foreign students representing over 70 countries.

Om orten.md: Queen's University is situated on a campus in the middle of the city of Kingston, which was founded more than 320 years ago. The city is located on the northeastern shore of Lake Ontario, about 3 hour bus trip from Toronto and Montreal and 2 hours from Ottawa. It is a relatively small city (about 146,000 inhabitants) and with many beautiful old buildings to their character not unlike Oxford in the UK. Students often live in a collective around the university. The city is also, due to its location on Lake Ontario and the archipelago, a tourist destination during the warm season.

The proximity to the Rocky Mountains provides excellent skiing opportunities. The cost of living is relatively low in Edmonton.

Om universitetet.md: The university was founded in 1903 as a branch of McGill University, but became an independent university in 1963 and currently has about 20,000 students. The university is well known for its interdisciplinary research and teaching centers and has a special environmental profile with a large number of courses in this area. The University also includes the well-known Bamfield Marine Station, where education is offered in marine biology / zoology. Students who wish to study at Bamfield Marine Station are especially recommended to take summer courses there, which is possible if one has a slightly lower rate of study during the fall and spring.

Om orten.md: The University of Victoria is beautifully located on Vancouver Island about eight kilometres outside the city of Victoria, the capital of the province of British Columbia. There is a well developed bus network between the University and the city of Victoria; by bus takes about 20 minutes to travel to Victoria from the university campus.The city of Victoria is a medium-sized Canadian city with about 320,000 inhabitants and is characterized by buildings in Victorian style. A wide range of cultural activities in art, music and theater are available. Victoria has Canada's mildest climate and is the only place in Canada where the palms grow outdoors year round. The mild climate allows one to conduct all sorts of outdoor sports year round, especially in football, rowing and grass hockey. For those who like skiing Whistler is about four hours away away.

Om orten.md:
As a Special Administrative Region of China, Hong Kong is situated on the southeast coast of China, occupying an area of 426 square miles (1,104 square kilometers). The city is one of the world's leading financial, banking and trading centers.

It is made up of four parts: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peninsula, the New Territories and the Outlying Islands. The prosperous island is the center of economy, politics, entertainment and shopping with its southern part noted for sea shores and bays. Kowloon is another flourishing part where Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Ma Tei and Mong Kok are the most popular destinations. The New Territories and Outlying Islands are ideal places to experience a peaceful and natural holiday.

The city has a population of over 7 million people and most (about 97% of the population) are Chinese and speak Cantonese and English. There are few language barriers, making the city one of the hottest travel destination in Asia.

Starting from Spring 2027, the university does not accept students of Chinese nationality (including Hong Kong and Macao) or from Taiwan.

Students will be assigned to a similar school/department and major at Fudan based on major at home university.  
Courses or programmes NOT open to exchange student: MBA, LLM (law), Medical, Special Programmes.

Fudan  
provides three different exchange programs. Students must choose ONLY ONE of  
them:

1. **Chinese Language Program**
- only taking Chinese Language  
courses at ICES (International Cultural Exchange School)

2. **General Advanced Program**
- taking undergraduate-level courses
- Students can select undergraduate courses from different schools/departments (courses in basic medical sciences, clinical medicine, nursing and other restricted programmes are not available).
- In general, General Advanced Program students CANNOT take Chinese Language Courses at ICES. Limited Chinese Language Courses at ICES and non-credit Chinese language training classes might be available in this program, but there is NO guarantee that they will be available every semester.

3. **Senior Advanced Program**
- taking EMA courses only: English-taught graduate-level courses
- ONLY School of International Relations and Public Affairs, and School of Philosophy offer EMA courses. Other schools/departments do NOT offer EMA courses

Om universitetet.md:
**Founded:** 1898

**Student Body:** 48 000

**Faculties/Colleges:** 55 schools and departments, 60 research entities

**Campus:** The campus, known as "Yan Yuan"（the garden of Yan, is situated at Haidian District in the western suburb of Beijing.

**Interesting Facts** : Peking University was originally known as the Imperial University of Peking. It was the first national university covering comprehensive disciplines in China and has been a leading institution of higher education in China since its establishment. It also served as the highest administration for education at the beginning of its founding.

The university adopted its present name in 1912. At the end of the 20th century, the Chinese government put Peking University at the top of its agenda for promoting higher education, with the aim to build a world-class university in the 21st Century. After merging with Beijing Medical University in 2000, Peking University once again was strengthened in its disciplinary structure.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
The university does not accept students of Chinese nationality (including Hong Kong and Macao) or from Taiwan.

Students should be above the age of 18 and under the age of 45.

Students in the graduate year at home university are NOT recommended to apply as official transcripts cannot be issued fast and it could affect exchange students’ graduation in their home university.  
The total English-taught graduate courses open to exchange students are very limited (less than 10 courses each semester).

For General Visiting Students, not proficient in Chinese, there are two options:

(1) Mainly study Chinese (from elementary to advanced levels). At the same time, students may take English-taught courses, if there is a requirement from the home university, of no more than 6 credits in total each semester at otherschools/departments (no department/school limit) if the courses and quotas are available.

(2) Give up Chinese language learning and only take English-taught courses (no department/school limit), please note that only few courses are available in English.

Students proficient in Chinese, may take undergraduate courses within or outside of their current major.

The following courses are not available for exchange students:

 English-taught graduate courses of special Master programmes (MBA, International Relations, Public Policy, LLM in Chinese Law, Yengching Academy etc).

 Health Science Center

 School of Software and Microelectronics

 Faculty with special pre-requisites

 Tailor-made programs

 Double-degree courses

 Shenzhen Graduate School (case-by-case discussion is needed)

 Courses opened by PKU Education

 Chinese-taught Master-level courses are only available with the faculty’s permit

Om universitetet.md:
**Founded:** 1911

**Student Body:** 42 000

**Faculties/Colleges:** Ten faculties with 59 departments and schools

**Interesting Facts:**

The University of Hong Kong is the oldest tertiary institution in Hong Kong. It was granted a shield and a motto by the College of Arms in 1913, and throughout its history the University's visual identity has been firmly based on their display, often coupled the University's name. This is a distinction that resonates outside Hong Kong, particularly in the United Kingdom, other Commonwealth jurisdictions, and the United States. It is also a reminder of the University's antiquity, and a most dignified and effective corporate identity.

Om orten.md:
As a Special Administrative Region of China, Hong Kong is situated on the southeast coast of China, occupying an area of 426 square miles (1,104 square kilometers).

The city is one of the world's leading financial, banking and trading centers. It is made up of four parts: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peninsula, the New Territories and the Outlying Islands. The prosperous island is the center of economy, politics, entertainment and shopping with its southern part noted for sea shores and bays. Kowloon is another flourishing part where Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Ma Tei and Mong Kok are the most popular destinations. The New Territories and Outlying Islands are ideal places to experience a peaceful and natural holiday.

The city has a population of 7 million people and most (about 97% of the population) are Chinese and speak Cantonese and English. There are few language barriers, making the city one of the hottest travel destination in Asia.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
**Faculty Restrictions**
- Faculty of Business and Economics (FBE): courses have become increasingly competitive and enrolment is not guaranteed for any specific course. Full FBE course loads are unlikely; students should not focus entirely on a single discipline within this Faculty. Backup courses are essential and students should be flexible in their study plan, or consider other faculties. Students must have a minimum CGPA of CGPA 3.0 (letter grade B).
- School of Computing and Data Science (SCDS), Faculty of Engineering: SCDS has extremely limited spots for accepting incoming students who have high academic grades. Application to SCDS will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Backup plans are essential and students should be flexible in their study plan, or consider other departments/faculties.
- Faculty of Law: students must be majoring in Law at their home institution. Students must have a minimum CGPA of 3.33 (equivalent to a B+)
- Common Core (CC) Courses: Highly recommended to explore global and local topics. Students can take up to two CC courses from a selective menu, each chosen from a different Area of Inquiry: 'Scientific and Technological Literacy', 'Humanities', 'Global Issues', and 'China: Culture, State and Society'.

Programmes or courses offered by the following Faculties are NOT opened to exchange students:

• Faculty of Dentistry  
• Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine  
• BSc (Exercise and Health) Programme  
• Postgraduate courses and most final year project courses provided by all faculties
- The approval of courses is on a case-by-case basis and subject to the Faculty's approval. Actual enrollment is subject to class availability, courses offered in the first semester, quota and class schedule. \[The information is subject to change without prior notice\]
- Students are recommended to check the course pre-requisites before selecting courses.
- 50% of the course load must be chosen from ONE faculty with the remaining credits from other faculties.

Språkkrav.md:
Unless English is the applicant’s first language and/or the teaching  
medium of home institution, applicant will need a recognised English  
Language qualification to be admitted into the exchange programme.

• Please refer to HKU's [English Language Requirement](https://admissions.hku.hk/apply/international-qualifications/english-language-requirement#C) & [English Proficiency Proof Requirement](https://intlaffairs.hku.hk/backend/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/HKU_English_Proficiency_Proof_Requirement-1.pdf) for the list of acceptable minimum qualifications.

• Please note the Faculty of Law has a higher requirement for English  
proficiency: TOEFL (iBT) 97  
or IELTS 7.0 (7.1 for Law) with no subtest below 6.5.

The test result can be submitted after the selection process.

For exchange studies in autumn semester, the deadline for submission of language test result is 1 March.

For exchange studies in spring semester, the deadline for submission of language test results is 1 August.

Boende.md:
Housing is not guaranteed, but the university can offer help finding [housing](https://housingfoundation.ku.dk/).

All exchange students automatically receive an invitation to apply for accommodation via Housing Foundation Copenhagen., but students can search for accommodation on their own. However, we do advise students to be careful, since there have been cases of students who have paid large deposits only to find out that the apartment did not belong to the person advertising it.

Please note that accommodation in Copenhagen is very expensive, with rent ranging from 4,000 to 10,000 DKK a month (and higher!).

It is also common practice in Denmark to pay 3 months’ rent in advance (typically this will be saved as the rent for the last 3 months of the rental period) as well as a deposit equal to 3 months' rent. This means that you will almost always have to pay a large sum of money in the beginning.

You can find more information and tips on searching for accommodation [here](https://studies.ku.dk/living-in-copenhagen/housing/)

Om universitetet.md:
Founded in 1632 by the Swedish King Gustav Adolf II, the University  
of Tartu (UT) is the oldest and largest university in Estonia both in  
terms of numbers of staff and students, and the volume of its teaching,  
research and development activities. As Estonia’s only classical  
university, UT embraces a wide variety of academic fields. Its current  
programme offer includes 60 bachelor, 72 master’s and 34 doctoral study  
programmes, including 18 degree programmes fully taught in English. As  
of 2015, its nine faculties and four associated colleges are home to  
close to 14,000 students and 1,500 academic staff. UT accounts for over  
half of Estonia’s national research output with close to 3,000 research  
articles published annually and 100 doctoral degrees conferred each  
year. According to the ISI Web of Science, UT belongs to the top 1% of  
the world’s most-cited universities and research institutions in 10  
fields. UT has cooperation agreements with 71 universities in 27  
countries and participates in the activities of several European  
university networks, such as the Utrecht Network and the Coimbra Group. UT alumni make up 40% of Estonian Parliament, 87% of attorneys at law, 100% of judges, and 99% of medical doctors in Estonia.

Om universitetet.md:
Sorbonne University was created on January 1st, 2018 from the merger of Paris-Sorbonne (founded in 1170) and Pierre and Marie Curie (UPMC) universities. As a public institution, it fulfils the public service calling of French higher education, research and innovation.  
The Faculty of Arts & Humanities at Sorbonne University is today the largest and most complete faculty in France, in the field of arts, languages, literature, social sciences and humanities. Committed to the transmission of a humanist culture, its pedagogical excel-lence is based on the recognized quality of its research to offer the most complete and in-novative teaching.

Språkkrav.md:
**A French language certificate of at least level B2 is mandatory** .

**NOTE!** **You must provide proof of French language proficiency at the time of application to Uppsala Univer** **sity** (15 November / 15 May).

If you do not have a valid French test result or a receipt for an upcoming language test in the application to Uppsala University, you can not be selected for Sorbonne Université. If you have a receipt and get selected by Uppsala University, you will receive a conditional offer until we receive the test results.

At Sorbonne University, most courses are  
taught in French, with the exception of certain language departments  
where courses are taught in both the learned language and French.  
Sorbonne  
University accepts students with a **B2 level** of French, however, a **C1  
level** is highly recommended for students who are not studying in a  
language department. Especially for those studying History, History of  
Art, Philosophy and Sociology, a good understanding of the French  
language is necessary.

The accepted language  
tests confirming the B2 level in French are as follows: **DALF, DELF,  
TCF, Alliance Française** . A signed certificate from a French  
teacher at the student's home university, which certifies that the student is able to follow a course and complete assignments/exams in French, is also accepted in combination with an OLS test result.

Om universitetet.md:
The University of Bordeaux campus is one of the largest in Europe (187

Om orten.md:
Bordeaux is located at the very heart of Southern Europe, only a few hours from major EU capitals and cities. Here are just some of the city’s greatest characteristics:

It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage List, described as "an outstanding urban and architectural ensemble”.  
It is a dynamic metropolis, blessed with a particularly prestigious historical and cultural heritage and is classified as "City of Art and History”.  
It is the wine capital of the world with around 10,000 wine-producing châteaux.  
Bordeaux is located just one hour from the Atlantic Ocean, thus enjoying a mild oceanic climate and rich natural surroundings.

Språkkrav.md:
**The University of Bordeaux requires students to be proficient in French as courses taught in English are very limited and full-time studies (30 ECTS) in English cannot be guaranteed. Students who do not speak French cannot apply to this university.**

**NOTE!** **You must provide proof of French language proficiency at the time of application to Uppsala Univer** **sity** (15 November / 15 May). **A minimum level of B1 or B2 (CEFR) is required, depending on the faculty. Please see the requirements below. Applications without a valid French test result or other proof of French language proficiency will not be considered for this exchange.**

• **Marketing Techniques, Transport Logistics Management, Business and Administration Management, Sustainable Towns and T** **erritories** : a certificate of minimum **level B1** (reading, writing, speaking) in French is required.  
• **Science and Technology** : a certificate of minimum **level B1** (reading, writing, speaking) in French is required.  
• **Health and Human Sciences, Education:** a certificate of minimum **level** **B2** (reading, writing, speaking) in French is required.

• **Law, Political Science** : a certificate of minimum **level B1** (reading, writing, speaking) in French is required.

• **Economics, Management:** **level B2** in French if your learning agreement has at least one course in French (official certificate or university letter/language teacher of less than 2 years accepted).

Om orten.md:
Tbilisi is located in southern Caucasus in eastern Georgia, on both sides of the river Kura. Tbilisi is the largest industrial and cultural center in Georgia.  
The average annual temperature in Tbilisi is 13° C. January is the coolest month with an average temperature of 2.3 ° C. July is the hottest month with an average temperature of 25 ° C.

Tbilisi has always been considered the great metropolis of the Caucasus. It is a city of ancient history, founded in the 5th-century, a fascinating mix of European and Asian cultures, a multi-ethnic, multi-cultural, multi-religious city.

Every corner of this welcoming place is full of stories and adventures. Tbilisi is home to major cultural events held in Georgia, starting from international exhibitions, concerts and festivals, extending to small-scale, extraordinary cultural celebrations found on tiny stages and squares throughout the city.

[Academic Calendar](https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/24440.html)

Please note that at the University of Göttingen, there is a distinction between the official semester dates (“Semesterzeit”) and the teaching period (“Vorlesungszeit”).

Exchange students are expected to stay until they complete all academic requirements, including classes, labs, and exams. In many cases, students can leave after their final exam or required on-site activity, which is often before the official semester end date. However, exam dates vary by department, and some students may need to stay longer. Many students return home once their exams are finished, but it is strongly recommend keeping travel plans flexible until exam dates are confirmed by the host department.

Om universitetet.md:
Founded in 1845, 17 000 students  
University of Galway is the largest and oldest University in the West of Ireland. More than 2,000 international students from over 90 countries, choose to study here. Over the past 170 years, University of Galway has built a distinguished reputation for teaching and research excellence in the fields of arts, social science, and celtic studies; business, public policy and law; engineering and informatics; medicine, nursing and health sciences; and science. University of Galway are ranked in the Top 2% of universities worldwide for the quality of their teaching and research. Research strengths include Biomedical Science and Engineering; Environmental Science, Marine science, Human rights law, Internet technology, digital humanities, social gerontology, child and family research.

Unique highlights include:  
The first UNESCO Chair in the Republic of Ireland, in Children, Youth and Civic Engagement  
The largest research institute for developing internet technology  
Ireland's primary stem cell and gene therapy research institute  
The world's leading experts in human rights law  
The campus itself is situated on the banks of the River Corrib, on one of the most attractive University sites in Europe. The original mid-nineteenth century university buildings are in the Tudor architectural style. The old stone quadrangle at the heart of the campus is flanked by new buildings, which reflect the steady growth of the University over the past decades.

University of Galway are ranked in the Top 2% of universities worldwide for the quality of their teaching and research. Research strengths include Biomedical Science and Engineering; Environmental Science, Marine science, Human rights law, Internet technology, digital humanities, social gerontology, child and family research. Unique highlights include: The first UNESCO Chair in the Republic of Ireland, in Children, Youth and Civic Engagement The largest research institute for developing internet technology Ireland's primary stem cell and gene therapy research institute The world's leading experts in human rights law The campus itself is situated on the banks of the River Corrib, on one of the most attractive University sites in Europe. The original mid-nineteenth century university buildings are in the Tudor architectural style. The old stone quadrangle at the heart of the campus is flanked by new buildings, which reflect the steady growth of the University over the past decades.

Om orten.md:
Galway is located on the doorstep of Connemara, the largest Gaeltacht (Irish-speaking area) in Ireland and an area of wild and majestic beauty. With its unique landscape of lakes, bogs and mountains, it is among the most evocative part of the country. Anyone wishing to experience the Ireland of rugged countryside, castles, lakes and rivers will not be disappointed; other attractions not far from the city are the Burren and the Aran Islands. King Richard III granted Galway its first Charter in 1484, and the town has been a seat of learning since the 1560s, when its merchant families founded an academy for students from all over Ireland. Traces of Galway's rich medieval past can still be seen today in the maze of winding medieval lanes and old merchants' mansions in the city centre.

Galway is now the third-largest city in the Republic, with a population of 76,000, almost 20% of which is made up of third-level students. The interdependence of town and University has helped to build a compact, thriving city that caters to young people like few other places can. Its youthful energy is reflected in the numerous internationally-renowned literary, arts and sporting events that are hosted there each year, such as the Cúirt International Festival of Literature, the Galway Film Fleadh, the Galway Arts Festival, and the Galway Racing Festival. Regarded by many as the cultural capital of Ireland, Galway is home to the well-known Druid Theatre Company, the Macnas Street Theatre Company and An Taibhdhearc, the national Irish-language theatre company.

A particular feature of Galway and its environs is the fact that, in addition to the city’s strong cosmopolitan atmosphere, the older Gaelic culture of Ireland - in music, song and language - is especially strong and vibrant in the western capital. This means that a visiting student can conduct all his/her business effectively and easily in English, but can also, if he or she wishes, encounter the richness of Ireland’s Celtic culture in all its forms.

Please be aware that students selected for an exchange to the University of Galway will be nominated to the same field of study they are studying at their home university. For example, students studying business at UU will be nominated to study business at the University of Galway.

Students are generally not permitted to take modules outside their area of study for which they have been nominated. Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
**Not available:** Due to different semester/ term systems, Keio Business School (KBS) Courses are not open to exchange students.

**1. Keio International Program (KIP)** :

Students can study about Japan and East/Southeast Asia by taking English-taught courses offered by the International Center.

In addition, KIP students may choose to take up to four (4) Japanese language courses each semester.

Please note there are different campuses and due to the distance (approximately 1.5 hours) between SFC and Tokyo, students enrolled in KIP@SFC are not permitted to take courses at other campuses.

**2. Japanese Language Program (JLP):**

An Intensive program for students (Japanese Language learners) who wish to focus on Japanese language Learning

**3. Graduate Studies Program (GSP)**

Intended for only master's degree students who wish to take graduate-level courses through affiliation with a Graduate School of Keio University.

**Restricted Courses:** Physical education courses, foreign language courses, and courses in the School of Medicine are not open to exchange students.

GPA requirement: All applicants MUST have at least a cumulative GPA of 3.0 / 4.0 or equivalent.

No exchanges can be extended. Plan and choose your study period carefully when applying for this exchange.

It's not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.

Read more here: fst.sophia.ac.jp/en/about

Department of Engineering and Applied Sciences - Green Engineering Program

The Green Engineering program is designed to provide electrical and mechanical engineering skills that will lead to the further development of energy-conservation technologies, efficient power generation, transmission and distribution.

Read more here: fst.sophia.ac.jp/en/about

\* In addition to the faculties listed above, many other faculties offer lecture courses taught in English. Students may take other lecture courses while being enrolled in the Faculty above.

**2. Graduate/master level**

Global Studies (GPGS)

The Graduate Program in Global Studies emphasizes inquiry into the contemporary world and its historical antecedents by combining the interdisciplinary themes of global studies, theories and the methods of academic disciplines, and cross-cultural understandings of Japanese and area studies.

It has three MA degrees - Global Studies, International Business and Development Studies, and Japanese Studies - each with its own specialized curriculum. Graduate exchange students are welcome to take content courses that are consistent with their graduate degree and for which they have sufficient background.

Read more here: sophia.ac.jp/eng/gpgs/

Global Environmental Studies (GES)

The curriculum covers three fields: Economics and Business Administration for the Environment, Law and Policies, Sociology for the Environment, and Science and Engineering for the Environment. One of the strategies of this program is to enhance the capacity of students to contribute to the solving of current environmental issues by offering them a wide variety of practical and discipline-specific programs.

Read more here: genv.sophia.ac.jp/english/index.html

Green Science and Engineering

Green Science and Engineering places an emphasis on environment- and sustainability-related studies, which are of paramount importance to the future of mankind. To foster cross-disciplinary education, faculty members drawn from all the other eight divisions (see details from website) are involved in the teaching.

Read more here: fst.sophia.ac.jp/en/graduate/igp

Linguistics (TESOL)

Program in Linguistics (TESOL) provides courses with an emphasis on both theory and practice. The faculty members represent a diverse spectrum of applied linguistics and language education, ensuring a comprehensive program for all who are interested in teaching English as a second or foreign language.

**3. Japanese Language Education**

Regular Track (4 credits)

The regular track offers beginning, intermediate to advanced courses where 100-minute classes meet four or five times per week. This course aims to focus on developing communicative competence through extensive practices by integrating four skills, listening, speaking, reading and writing. English is occasionally used for instruction as necessary.

Intensive Track (8 credits)

Intensive Japanese track, which offers four-level intensive courses at beginning, intermediate, and advanced levels, is designed for students whose main purpose of coming to Japan is to study Japanese. Classes meet for three hours a day through Monday to Friday. Fifteen hours of class time per week allow students to spend sufficient time to gain the high level of Japanese proficiency. English is occasionally used for instruction as necessary.

Japanese Language Education

**The following courses are NOT open to Exchange Students.**
- FLA core programs
- FST laboratory classes
- GPGS compulsory courses
- the foreign language courses (except Japanese language)
- Seminars except FLA
- Courses in Studies in Christian Humanism
- Compulsory courses in General Studies, “Studies in Christian Humanism: For Others, with Others”, “Liberal Arts of the Body”, “Critical Thinking & Writing”, “Overview of Data Science”, “Thinking about Issues, Perspectives and Positionality”.
- Academic English courses under University-wide General Studies (Courses with registration codes that start from GSP and the numberings with ENG)

Exchange students should mainly take courses offered by their own faculties and programs. Exchange students must register and attend more than 10 hours of classes per week. To fulfill this requirement, attending at least 6 periods (100 minutes constitute one period) every week is necessary.

Om universitetet.md:
Founded in 1877, the University of Tokyo (UTokyo) is the oldest national university in Japan. Over the course of its long and distinguished history, the university has produced some of the most outstanding scholars, scientists, and social and political leaders of Japan and the world, including eight Nobel laureates, 16 prime ministers of Japan, and one Fields Medal winner.

As Japan’s most comprehensive research university, UTokyo has ten undergraduate faculties, 15 graduate schools and 26 research institutes. More than 5,800 faculty members teach approximately 14,000 undergraduate students and almost equal number of graduate students at three main campuses in the Tokyo region and additional research facilities across Japan. UTokyo is committed to excellence in research and education as well as establishing a truly global campus to produce the next generation of leaders of the world.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
Level restrictions:  
**Student exchange is only  
available for undergraduate students.** Type U is  
primarily designed for admitting undergraduate students. However, it is  
possible for graduate students who intend to take only  
undergraduate-level courses at UTokyo to apply.  
If you plan to graduate before or right after your exchange period, you are not eligible for this program

Course Restrictions:

USTEP Type U students are allowed to take up to two credit-bearing Japanese  
language classes per week.

(Students who request to take three credit-bearing Japanese language courses  
per week must get special permission by including a document filled out by their  
home university in the online application process to Tokyo). Please note  
that a course offered twice a week counts as two classes. There are no  
restrictions on non-credit-bearing Japanese language programs offered by the  
Japanese Language Education Division. ([https://globe.u-tokyo.ac.jp/nkc/en/index.html](https://globe.u-tokyo.ac.jp/nkc/en/index.html))

Some non-credit- bearing courses are offered by Faculty of Engineering.  
Please  
observe that course restrictions may pose challenges for students whose  
primary academic focus is Japanese language learning.

Study program:

USTEP Program Open to undergraduate students.  
The Type U program is  
designed for undergraduate students to take courses given in English  
and/or Japanese at the undergraduate College and Faculties.  
In principle, first and second year undergraduate  
students are not accepted for USTEP. For students enrolled in three-year  
undergraduate programs, they must have finished at least 1.5-year of the  
program at the time of their arrival at UTokyo.

Please check your eligibility before applying for a place to this  
university:  
[https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep-type-u.html  
https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep-overview.html](https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/academics/ustep-type-u.html)

**It's not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have  
completed your studies.**

**To be selected to this university, you need to have very good grades!**

Språkkrav.md:
English/Japanese test required. The Type U program requires exchange students to meet the language requirements in English and/or Japanese, depending on the courses they wish to take.

Students who wish to take courses offered in English:
- A minimum TOEFL iBT score of 90
- IELTS overall band score of 6.5
- Cambridge English Qualifications "C1 Advanced"
- Duolingo English Test (DET) score of 120.

\*TOEFL iBT Home Edition, IELTS Online / One Skill Retake are accepted.

\*TOEFL iBT “MyBest Scores” is not accepted.

\*TOEFL iBT, IELTS and DET scores are valid only if dated within two years of the USTEP application deadline.

or
- Attend a university or have graduated from a high school where the medium of instruction is English

\*Applicants must submit a proof that certifies that the degree program they belong to is taught entirely in English, unless they attend a university in an English-speaking country or are a native speaker of the language

(\*A native speaker is defined here as someone who graduated from a high school where the medium of instruction is English).

Students who wish to take courses offered in Japanese:
- JLPT Level N1

or
- Have graduated from a high school where the medium of instruction is in Japanese.

The test result should be submitted per email to mobility@uu.se.

For exchange studies in autumn semester, the deadline for submission of language test result is 1 February.

For exchange studies in spring semester, the deadline for submission of language test result is 1 September.

**Please observe: The University of Tokyo expects its exchange students to study specialized subjects during their exchange study, so at least one of the classes a student takes must be a non-language class. Therefore, even if you would like to mainly study Japanese language, you must submit a proof for the required language proficiency.**

Om universitetet.md: Tohoku University was founded in 1907 as the third imperial university, during the period when Japan had begun to transform itself into a modernized society. Since then, it has played a leading role in both research and education in Japan, and is now ranked among the top universities in the Asia-Pacific region. From the start Tohoku University has maintained uniqueness within Japan. The university has always conceived strong loyalty to science while other former imperial universities have tried to meet the governmental needs. Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
Available exchange programs:

**Undergraduate studies**

**1. Junior Year Program in English (JYPE)**
- Fields: Science, Engineering, Agriculture (3rd year only)

The core course (required) of this program is an Individual Research Training (IRT) course, where undergraduate students will research, with the support of research groups to which the students are assigned, in a current topic that is related to their field of studies.

Jype has a high level of study, and is thus only recommended to students  
devoted to their studies and prepared for hours of hard work in the  
research course.

**2. International Program in Liberal Arts (IPLA)**
- Fields: Humanities/Social Sciences (2nd or 3rd year only)- Read more here: [http://www.insc.tohoku.ac.jp/english/exchange/ipla/](http://www.insc.tohoku.ac.jp/english/exchange/ipla/)

**Postgraduate/master studies**

1. Cooperative Laboratory Study Program ( **COLABS)**
- Fields: All Natural Sciences, Engineering, Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy - Read more here: [http://www.insc.tohoku.ac.jp/english/exchange/colabs/](http://www.insc.tohoku.ac.jp/english/exchange/colabs/)

Nota bene! COLABS: Only free-standing master students with a bachelor’s degree (180 credits or more) or integrated bachelor/master (300hp) with at least 180 credits at the time of the application.

For Autumn semester application: Have 180hp already in December/January as Tohoku has an early deadline in February. The deadline for the COLABS Prior Consent Request Application is January 30th. No extensions to the application period will be granted.

COLABS applicant must be:
- a full-time registered degree seeking student, during participating in COLABS, at graduate level with excellent grades at the home university
- remain a full-time registered degree seeking student at graduate level at the home university after completing the COLABS program at Tohoku University.

**It is not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.**

Note that each program has certain policies regarding the time of enrollment (some programs accept Fall enrollment only), and students cannot change their program once enrolled.

Om orten.md: Almaty is located in the south east of Kazakhstan and with a population of about 1.5 million people it is the biggest city in Kazakhstan (it was the capital city up until 1998, now it is Astana). It is the hub of the country's trade and culture and is also considered to be one of the most beautiful cities of Central Asia. Located in the foothills of the Zailishkiy Alatau Mountains with its skating rink, Medeo, and skiing resort, Chymbulak, the city is surrounded with beautiful nature such as the Kulsay lakes, Charyn canyon, and sandy dunes in the National Park Altyn-Emel. Almaty is described as a pleasant city to live in, vibrant, green, and with a thriving cosmopolitan culture. The spectacular mountains are only half an hour’s drive from the city center. July is the hottest month in Almaty with average temperature of 30°C and the coldest month being January with around -15°C. There are some rainy days in spring and summer (the rainiest month is April with an average rainfall of 80 mm) but all seasons are said to be pleasant.

Ewha has now grown into one of Korea’s most prestigious schools and the world’s largest women’s university. Ewha is still true to its core values and students are expected to attend chapel once a week.

Although a women's university, men are accepted for exchange studies.

Om universitetet.md:
**Founded:** 1905

**Student Body:** 40,000

**Faculties/Colleges:** 51 schools

**Collaborations/Networks:** SKY is an unofficial grouping and acronym for the three most prestigious and academically competitive universities located in Seoul, South Korea. It consists of Seoul National University, Korea University, and Yonsei University.

**Interesting Fact:** Korea University (KU, Hangul: 고려대학교; hanja: 高麗大學校; RR: Goryeo Daehakgyo) is a research institution and one of the nation's oldest institutions of higher education. The university’s academic breadth is extensive, with 95% of full-time faculty members holding Ph.D. or equivalent qualification in their field.

The university is notable in South Korean history for being the first educational institution to offer academic programs in various disciplines, such as law, economics, and journalism.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
Graduate students will be considered for exchange studies on master level on a case-by-case basis but are welcome to take courses on a bachelor's level if that is an option. If the student must study on masters level during exchange studies, it is advisable to apply for a different university.

Non-available subjects to students: Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Law, Teacher Education, Cyber Defense, Art & Design, Smart Mobility, Communication Engineering and all courses at Sejong Campus are not open to exchange students.

Graduate School of International Studies> courses are not available to undergraduate exchange students.

Registration for courses from Business School, Media & Communications, Psychology and International Studies (courses that start with BUSS, JMCO, DISS and PSYC) is extremely competitive. Graduate programs at the Business School are not open to exchange students.

IMPORTANT

• Undergraduates must have completed a minimum of 2 semesters (Postgraduates: 1 semester) at home institution before application to KU starts.

• Must submit a transcript for more than 2 semesters ((Transcript including the second semester that is issued during or after application period is not acceptable)

• A minimum GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (GPA by US standard  
• You need to be enrolled at Uppsala University the semester before the exchange starts.

Students with Korean heritage, may have Korean nationality still active, which could result in their visa application being rejected.

**It's not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.**

**On-campus housing** is not guaranteed, but students are eligible to apply for on-campus housing (on first come first serve basis)

Students apply for housing online at [dorm.korea.ac.kr/](https://dorm.korea.ac.kr/) (Frontier, CJ/Anam International House).

Students who are assigned on-campus housing will be required to take a tuberculosis test (x-ray, blood test or skin test), in January (for Spring semester) and July (for Autumn semester) or after. Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
All applicants for exchange program must choose one college and department as their affiliation and in general, applicants choose one that most suits their academic background or study abroad purpose. However, if a large number of students apply to a particular department, it is possible that some may not pass the first round of screening. In such cases, applicants will be re-evaluated based on their second-choice department and may be required to change their choice if SNU. (For your reference, the College of Liberal Studies and School of Transdisciplinary innovations are among the departments with higher acceptance rates) Regardless, students can choose courses even outside their major/department at SNU.

\*Note: Some courses may have restrictions

**Exchange students are not accepted to the following departments/schools**
- College of Business Administration (Graduate School)
- Deptartment of Computer Science and Engineering
- Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
- Department of Economics (Graduate School) in the College of Social Sciences
- Department of Political Science and International Relations (Graduate School) in the College of Social Sciences

**Restrictions** **apply for the following** **departments/schools**
- The following disciplines: Medicine, Pharmacy, Dentistry, Nursing, Music and Fine Arts, require prior agreement.
- Departments of Korean History/Psychology/Statistics: applicants must provide proof of Korean language proficiency. A satisfactory level of Korean language ability should be Level 5 or above of the official Korean Language Proficiency Test, TOPIK.
- College of Law is NOT open to undergraduate level students. School of Law, a specialized law school for graduate level students, will be open to undergraduate level students and students will be enrolled as graduate (Master’s) students in SNU law school during their study.
- Graduate School of Business (MBA program) is only offered for the Spring semester and restricted to current full-time MBA students at home university. Please note that it is very limited in spaces, prior agreement is needed and an application is likely to be rejected. The academic system of MBA program differs from other programs (Details to be individually announced from the MBA coordinator). For further information about MBA courses, please visit SNU GSB website at [gsb.snu.ac.kr.](https://uu-bo.moveon4.de/gsb.snu.ac.kr.)

GSIS applicants must have a recommendation letter when applying to SNU.

Undergraduate students must have completed two semesters of studies and graduate students the first semester of the Master’s program at the time of application to SNU.

**It's not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.**

The literal meaning of the university’s name is, “An institution for building a harmonious society of perfected human beings.” The founding philosophy of SKKU was needed then as much as it is needed in today’s technologically advanced society. The university is committed to quality teaching and research, offering students a challenging environment for intellectual and personal growth.

SKKU is a world-class center of higher education with over 600 years of history. Since its founding at the dawn of the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910), SKKU has demonstrated strong academic leadership. In fact, in all core disciplines, SKKU actively encourages global research and collaboration through academic exchange of faculty and students, and the development of innovative educational and research programs with global partners.

Om universitetet.md:
**Founded:** 1885

**Student Body:** 30 000 undergraduate and 12 000 postgraduate students.

**Faculties/Colleges** : 32 colleges and graduate schools

**Campus:** Spread over three sites situated in Sinchon, Wonju and its state-of-the-art international campus in Songdo.

**Collaborations/Networks:** SKY is an unofficial grouping and acronym for the three most prestigious and academically competitive universities located in Seoul, South Korea. It consists of Seoul National University, Korea University, and Yonsei University.

**Interesting Facts:** Yonsei University was founded by Horace Grant Underwood, a Christian missionary. It had many identities before becoming Yonhi University in 1946, taking on its current name in the late 1950s. Yonsei is regarded as South Korea’s top private university.

The university was founded on Christian principles, and this is still a prominent part of its mission, which states its dedication to “educate future leaders of our society in the spirit of Christianity, fostering a strong and lasting commitment to the principles of truth and freedom.”

Despite these wonders, the town also features all the comforts of a modern city. Ifrane boasts a fair number of delicious restaurants, whose gastronomy varies from traditional Moroccan and Lebanese cuisines, to Mexican and Japanese restaurants, to cafés, an array of shops, and some nightlife options

Om orten.md:
The ancient Hanseatic city of Groningen, with 200,000 inhabitants is  
situated in the north of the Netherlands. As the economic and cultural  
capital of the region, the city enjoys a bustling reputation, while  
retaining a safe community character. Full of restaurants, pubs, art  
galleries, theatres, museums and bookshops Groningen is suited to its  
youthful population, and its inner-city markets and wide variety of  
shops attract a great number of regional and German visitors every day.  
The university has a visible presence: the historic buildings in the  
inner-city tell the tale of a rich academic tradition, while the  
University Medical Center Groningen is an example of ground-breaking  
architecture. A great number of students are enjoying sports, and  
cultural events and festivals at reasonable prices. The city has a  
varied population and its shops, restaurants and places of worship cater  
to every ethnic background.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
This is an all-field agreement except Medicine, Dentistry, and Pharmacy. Certain restrictions apply, though, so check the course catalogue carefully!

Please observe that you must take most of your courses at the same faculty. It can be difficult to match courses from two different faculties.

**For Psychology, Sociology, Philosophy** **and Education** : You should have studied the subject for a year at least and to be nominated to this faculty you need to have Psychology, Sociology, Philosophy or Education as your major subject at Uppsala University. There are not enough Psychology courses on first-year level covering a full semester. For studies at master level, you need to have the English level of C1.

**For Business and Economics:** To be accepted, students need to have taken a minimum of 10-12 courses (60 ECTS) in the field of economics and business. Students should have covered subjects such as statistics, microeconomics, macroeconomics, (financial) accounting and research methods.

**For Law:** You must have studied law for two years before the exchange. Please observe that you must take most of your courses within the same faculty. Up to approx. 2 courses can be taken within another faculty. For studies at master level, you need to have the English level of C1.

It's not certain that it is possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.

The University of Groningen does not provide housing for students. There is currently a housing shortage in general especially among students. The housing shortage is very persistent, particularly in the first semester (September – January).

The University of Groningen can not wholly or partially refund housing contracts signed between the student and SSH in case of (late) cancellation of the exchange by the student, or early or intermediate termination of the stay in Groningen/rental agreement. [https://www.athomeingroningen.com/](https://www.athomeingroningen.com/)  
[https://www.rug.nl/education/exchange/study-in-groningen/](https://www.rug.nl/education/exchange/study-in-groningen/)

Please note that at this moment, there are serious housing problems. If a student is unable to find accommodation before the start of their exchange, the University of Groningen strongly advise to cancel the exchange.

Visum och uppehållstillstånd.md: If you are a non-EU student, you will need a [visa and/or residence permit](https://www.rug.nl/feb/education/exchange/incoming/practical-information/visa). In order to obtain a visa/residence permit, the Immigration and Naturalization Service will check whether you have sufficient financial resources to support yourself during your stay in the Netherlands. The Immigration and Naturalization Service considers about € 950 per month (which is about € 6000 for a semester) sufficient. Students need to pay the entire amount of € 6000 in advance to get the visa/residence permit.

Om universitetet.md: The University of Otago is New Zealand's oldest university, founded in 1869. It has earned an international reputation for the quality of its research and teaching. Teaching at Otago is closely related to scholarly research, with the result that most teaching is undertaken by academics at the forefront of relevant knowledge. As a student at New Zealand's oldest university you will become part of a unique educational experience. Otago's attractive campus is a mixture of historic and modern buildings located in the centre of Dunedin. The campus is a short walk from the city's central shopping and services.

Om orten.md: Dunedin is a city by the sea. It has white sand beaches, bush clad hills, tidal inlets and volcanic landforms. The heart of the city is lined with restaurants and sidewalk cafes. Modern shopping complexes trade alongside boutiques, galleries and craft markets. Nature endowed Dunedin with coastal colonies of the shy Yellow- eyed penguins, and the world's only mainland breeding colony of the Royal Albatross. Dunedin's green belt and its many parks and gardens add to the breath and soul of the city. The 'kiwi' passion for water sports is met by Dunedin's long natural harbour - ideal for wind surfing, yachting, kayaking, canoeing, rowing and fishing. Surf's up all year round on Dunedin’s beaches. St Clair beach is considered one of New Zealand's best for surfing.

Some Otago courses such as MBA, Wildlife Management and Master of Science Communication are restricted in admissions.

Apart from the above programmes, students coming to Otago on exchange will be accepted into any courses they meet the prerequisites for – there is no cap on the number of students accepted to a particular course.

Om universitetet.md:
Victoria has 4 main campuses, three of which are all within 15 minutes walk from each other in the city, in the midst of the cafes, galleries, and shops.  
Victoria University is a research-led university with high standards of teaching, which attracts exceptional staff and students from around the world. As a capital city university, Victoria has strong links with government departments and agencies, international agencies, industries, regional and local government, iwi and environmental organisations, as well as some of New Zealand’s major research institutes. The University also has extensive collaborative and student exchange links with renowned universities throughout the Pacific, Asia, North and South America and Europe.

Quick Facts:  
Top 1% of the world’s universities in 17 subject areas. Top 2% of the world’s 18,000 universities.  
Victoria Business School is among just 1% of business schools worldwide that hold the rare triple crown of international accreditations.  
3 main campuses, which are all within a 15-minute radius in the city, in the midst of the cafes, galleries, and shops.  
Over 22,000 students, including 3,000 international students.

A final grade of 4/VG or 15/C in English (A or B) in the Avgångsbetyg, or Slutbetyg; or a grade of C or higher in English (5 or 6) in the Högskoleförberedande examen according to: [Apply | Undergraduate Study Abroad or Exchange (international students) | Victoria University of Wellington (wgtn.ac.nz)](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/explore/other-quals/study-abroad-and-exchange/apply-contact?programme=study-abroad-and-exchange&international=true)

If you do not have the required results from Upper Secondary School proof a TOEFL or IELTS test may be required:

TOEFL - minimum score of 80 for the internet-based test. Please have your testing centre send results to directly to Victoria University of Wellington (Victoria Institution code = 9485, department code = 00).

IELTS - minimum overall score of 6.0 with no sub score below 5.5 (must be the academic test paper);

PTE - 58 with a minimum of 50 in a ‘Communicative’ score

If you’re planning to study teaching, you need to have a minimum IELTS overall band of 7.0 with no sub-score below 7.0.

Boende.md:
Student Accommodation at Victoria University of Wellington is very competitive. This means that students may not be placed in one of their initial choices for accommodation.

Mature students or students who have experience living away from home are advised to consider the self-catered halls of residence. All students over the age of 20 will be offered a self-catered hall only.

Exchange students will need a reference but should not need a financial guarantor.

All international students are automatically signed up to the [Studentsafe Inbound University insurance](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/international/get-ready-to-study/insurance) and pay for this upon enrolment at Victoria University of Wellington. This policy provides comprehensive cover throughout the course of study, and also covers the insured student’s travel to New Zealand and time spent in New Zealand up to 31 days before the start of their courses. This retrospective cover is provided automatically, irrespective of whether the student has paid the insurance premium in advance or not.

Avgifter.md:
Students must pay for a [Student's Pass](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/life-at-ntu/student-life/student-services/onestop/student's-pass) (STP) by the Singapore Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) for the duration of the programme.

NTU will also charge a non-refundable miscellaneous and administrative fee of approximately S\$410 (Undergraduate) or S\$470 (Postgraduate), inclusive of GST, payable by all exchange applicants after accepting the Offer and by the second week of the semester. This fee contributes to the costs associated with providing student insurance, programmes and amenities, IT services, academic-related resources, administrative and onboarding support, as well as social activities for inbound students during their period of immersion at NTU. Miscellaneous fees for the second semester will also apply for students nominated for full year exchange.

Please also see information under Insurance and Vaccination/Health requirements.

Ämnesbegränsningar.md:
All incoming students are advised to be as flexible as possible with their module requirements. There are no guarantees for any modules at NUS, and some modules are in high demand and will be difficult to register for.

To be eligible, students must have higher than average grades, the equivalent to an average B-grade at NUS with no grade lower than a C (NUS grading scale is A - F and B is approx. GPA 3.3).

Business courses are not offered to exchange students under this university-wide agreement.  
Only limited spaces are offered for Law students and cannot be guaranteed (however, students nominated for Law exchange must take at least 2 courses from NUS Law). Please note that no Law places are available for Autumn 2027.

Courses in Architecture, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, and Economics are in high demand and places are limited.

Courses from the following Faculties/Schools/Institutes/Departments are NOT open to any Non-Graduating applicants/ students:

• Faculty of Dentistry

• Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine (module codes that do not start with LSM only)

• Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health (Graduate courses only)

• Alice Lee Centre for Nursing Studies

• Institute of Systems Science

• All courses offered by self-funded programmes

• In the past, there have been extremely high demand from exchange students for Architecture and Computer Science courses which make enrolment into these courses extremely competitive.

See more about course restrictions: [nus.edu.sg/registrar/docs/info/prospective-students---non-graduating/non-graduating-course-restrictions.pdf](https://nus.edu.sg/registrar/docs/info/prospective-students---non-graduating/non-graduating-course-restrictions.pdf)

Exchange students should select Level 1000 – 4000 courses and will not be considered for level 5000 – 6000 graduate courses.

It's not possible to go to this university on an exchange after you have completed your studies.
